high.title: Vietnam Stock Market Awaits Major September Event: ~$128M in Vietnamese Equities Could Enter FTSE Radar
high.summary: Vietnam's landmark FTSE Russell Emerging Market (EM) upgrade takes effect on **21 September 2026**, with the eligible stock list to be officially published on **21 August 2026**. ACBS Securities estimates **19 stocks** will qualify for inclusion in the FTSE Global Equity Index Series (FTSE GEIS), comprising 4 large-cap, 1 mid-cap, and 14 small-cap names based on data through 30 June 2026. Estimated **net passive inflows for the September rebalancing are approximately USD 128 million (~VND 3,371 billion)**, with Vingroup (VIC) leading at ~USD 60.08 million (~VND 1,580 billion), followed by Vinhomes (VHM).

high.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of July 15: Survey Across Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank and Others
high.summary: The latest deposit rate survey (as of July 15, 2026) reveals that the upper end of the Vietnamese banking system's retail deposit curve remains elevated, with ACB leading at 7.30% p.a. for 12-month tenors, followed by Saigonbank at 7.20% and Bac A Bank at 7.10%. A total of six banks now quote rates at or above 7.00% for the 12-month tenor, including MBV, VCBNeo, and VIB. The next tier — LPBank, BVBank, OCB, and PGBank — clusters at 6.90% for 12-month deposits.

high.title: Bank Deposit Rates as of July 14: ACB Leads Market at 7.3%/Year for 12-Month Term
high.summary:
The Vietnamese deposit rate landscape continues to show upward pressure at the retail level, with ACB maintaining the highest advertised rate in the market at 7.3%/year for 12-month tenors, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2% and Bac A Bank at 7.1%. Notably, seven banks are now offering 7.0% or above on 12-month deposits — a meaningful cluster signaling competitive pressure to attract VND liquidity. MBV and VCBNeo (digital banking arms) are offering a flat 7.0% curve across 6–18 month maturities, suggesting yield curve flatness at the retail level. The four state-owned commercial banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) remain at lower levels, reflecting their dominant deposit franchise and implicit SBV guidance. For bond investors, these elevated retail deposit rates act as a floor and competing benchmark for government bond yields — if deposit rates stay elevated at 7%+, demand for government bonds at sub-7% yields may face headwinds. FX traders should monitor whether rising deposit rates are drawing VND back into the banking system, which could reduce dollarization pressures. Watch whether the SBV signals any guidance to moderate rates in the near term.

---

medium.title: VinaCapital Expert Speaks Candidly About the Paradox in Vietnam's Stock Market
medium.summary:
VinaCapital's Senior Investment Director, Dinh Duc Minh, highlights a notable disconnect in Vietnamese equities: **excluding Vingroup-related stocks, the VN-Index has effectively declined ~5% year-to-date**, while average daily liquidity has halved to approximately USD 500 million per session. This contrasts sharply with underlying corporate fundamentals — HoSE-listed company profits rose ~37% YoY in Q1 2026, with VinaCapital projecting a further 15–20% growth in Q2. The expert attributes the dislocation to concurrent macro headwinds weighing on investor sentiment. For international fund managers, the compression in valuations — despite solid earnings growth — may present a selective entry opportunity, though thin liquidity conditions warrant caution on position sizing.

---

medium.title: Vietnamese Equities Drop 150 Points from Peak — Is the Bottom Forming?
medium.summary:
The VN-Index has lost approximately 150 points from its recent peak, falling below the 1,800-point level to its lowest level in nearly three months. Since the start of July 2026, the index has shed close to 100 points. According to Luong Duy Phuoc, Head of Market Research at Kafi Securities, the correction reflects a confluence of external and domestic pressures. On the external side, escalating US-Iran geopolitical tensions drove Brent crude from ~$72/bbl to above $82/bbl rapidly, stoking inflation fears and raising expectations that the Fed will keep rates higher for longer — directly dampening risk appetite and capital flows into emerging markets including Vietnam. Domestically, foreign investors have maintained sustained net selling, and domestic liquidity has weakened materially, reinforcing the downward momentum. Analysts are now watching whether technical support levels will hold and whether any stabilization in global risk sentiment could trigger a reversal of foreign outflows from Vietnamese equities.

**Relevance:** Sustained foreign net selling on the VN-Index is a leading indicator of capital outflow pressure, which has direct implications for VND stability and SBV FX intervention dynamics. A prolonged equity drawdown combined with foreign outflows could test the VND and prompt SBV to reassess its intervention posture.

medium.title: Banking Sector H1 2026 Earnings Update (July 15): More Banks Report Surging Profits
medium.summary: Vietbank reported preliminary H1 2026 pre-tax profit of VND 923 billion, a sharp 79.4% year-on-year increase, driven primarily by net interest income growth of 26% to VND 1,747 billion. Total assets surpassed VND 205 trillion (+4% YTD), loan book grew 11% to VND 120.3 trillion, and customer deposits rose 5.6% to VND 132.4 trillion. BVBank also reported estimated total asset growth of approximately 7% versus end-2025. Both banks are tracking ahead of their full-year targets. The strong profitability across smaller and mid-tier banks reflects the current high-rate environment benefiting net interest margins, while credit growth remains robust. For bond and FX investors, healthy bank earnings reduce systemic risk concerns but also suggest credit demand remains strong — a factor the SBV will monitor closely when calibrating any future rate easing moves.

medium.title: Vietnam's Seafood Exports Surge — China Surpasses the US as Top Buyer
medium.summary: Vietnam's seafood exports totaled over $5.7 billion in H1 2026, up 11.4% year-on-year, according to the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment. China emerged as the top destination, importing nearly $1.4 billion worth of Vietnamese seafood — a ~40% increase versus the same period last year — surpassing the US ($898 million). Including Hong Kong, the Greater China region absorbed ~$1.5 billion (+38%). Japan ranked third at ~$788 million. **Relevance:** Strong export performance, particularly the pivot toward Chinese demand, is a modest positive for Vietnam's trade balance and current account, which in turn supports the VND. The diversification away from US-concentrated export risk is also worth noting given ongoing global trade policy uncertainty. This data point contributes to the broader balance-of-payments picture that fund managers should incorporate into VND positioning.

medium.title: VinaCapital Investment Director: Vietnamese Should Consider Allocating Around 2/3 of Assets to Equities
medium.summary:
Speaking at a VinaCapital-organized event, Mr. Thai Quang Trung, CFA, Chief Investment Officer and Fund Manager at VinaCapital, noted that despite Vietnamese equities trading at attractive valuations with strong long-term growth potential, most Vietnamese retail investors remain significantly underweight in equities. According to VinaCapital's own survey, Vietnamese household equity holdings amount to only roughly one-tenth the scale of real estate investment. Total retail equity holdings (excluding insider/corporate stakes) are estimated at approximately one-third of GDP, versus real estate values several multiples of GDP. Mr. Trung attributed this underallocation primarily to the short-term volatility of the Vietnamese equity market, which deters retail participation. For international fund managers, this commentary is relevant as a structural signal: a gradual reallocation of domestic capital from real estate into Vietnamese equities — even a modest shift — could serve as a significant medium-term demand catalyst for the VN-Index. Monitoring domestic retail investor sentiment and fund inflow data will be important to assess whether this structural shift is materializing.

---

medium.title: VinaCapital Expert: Stock Deployment Opportunity Has Emerged
medium.summary: VinaCapital's Senior Investment Director, Dinh Duc Minh, stated at a recent VinaCapital-hosted event that sentiment in the Vietnamese stock market remains cautious, with investment performance over the past 6–12 months falling short of investor expectations. He argued that periods of weak sentiment and compressed valuations — not periods of euphoria — represent the lower-risk entry points for equity accumulation, citing the market peaks of early 2018 and early 2022 as cautionary examples. For VN-Index watchers, this signals that a major domestic institutional voice is turning constructive on equities amid subdued liquidity. Improved equity sentiment could attract incremental domestic capital flows into the market, with potential spillover effects on broader risk appetite. International fund managers should monitor whether this view gains traction and whether a re-rating of Vietnamese equities follows, which could also influence foreign portfolio inflows into the VN-Index.

medium.title: Four "Diamond" Stocks Once Favored by Foreign Investors: FPT and PNJ Losing Appeal
medium.summary: This article examines the shifting foreign investor appetite toward four historically premium Vietnamese stocks — FPT, MWG, REE, and PNJ — which were once at full foreign ownership room and commanded significant premiums on block trades. Recent data as of July 16 suggests foreign ownership room in these names has opened up, indicating net foreign selling or reduced demand. For FX and capital flow watchers, a sustained retreat by foreign investors from previously coveted Vietnamese equities could represent a broader signal of weakening foreign portfolio inflows into the VN-Index, with potential mild negative pressure on VND through reduced equity-related USD conversion demand. The structural relevance to VNDiamond ETF flows also warrants monitoring.

medium.title: Securities Company Data Update July 17: First Loss in the Securities Sector Appears in Q2/2026
medium.summary: Nine securities companies have now reported Q2/2026 pre-tax earnings. EVS Securities posted a strong Q2 pre-tax profit of VND 243 billion (vs. a VND 9 billion loss in Q2/2025), driven almost entirely by FVTPL financial asset gains of VND 278 billion — over 13x year-on-year. Maybank Securities Vietnam also reported solid results with Q2 pre-tax profit of VND 68 billion (+35% YoY). However, the article notes that the first industry loss for Q2/2026 has also emerged within the cohort. Mixed securities sector results reflect the uneven trading environment on the VN-Index. Weak brokerage revenue could signal subdued retail participation and lower liquidity — a medium-term negative for equity market depth that international investors should track.

medium.title: H1 2026 Bank Earnings Update (July 16): One Bank Reports ~VND 4,700bn Half-Year Profit; VietBank and ABBank Surge
medium.summary: Three mid-tier banks reported strong H1 2026 earnings. TPBank posted pre-tax profit of VND 4,668bn, up 12.5% YoY, with credit growth of 9.62% and NPL ratio held below 1.5% — broadly healthy fundamentals. VietBank delivered a standout 79.4% YoY profit surge to VND 923bn, driven by 26% growth in net interest income; total assets exceeded VND 205,000bn with loan growth of 11%. The broad-based earnings momentum across the banking sector supports positive sentiment for bank equities on the VN-Index and suggests credit conditions remain accommodative despite elevated deposit rates. Investors should note that NIM sustainability will be a key risk to monitor in H2 if funding costs continue rising.

medium.title: New Bank Stock Ticker Debuts: PVcomBank Lists as "PCB" on UPCoM
medium.summary: PVcomBank has received approval from the Hanoi Stock Exchange (HNX) to list 900 million ordinary shares on UPCoM under the ticker PCB, with a par value total of VND 9,000bn. The bank reported 2025 consolidated pre-tax profit of VND 1,704bn and total assets of VND 263,457bn (up 17% YoY). This brings the total number of listed bank stocks in Vietnam to 28 across HOSE, HNX, and UPCoM. The listing expands the investable banking universe for portfolio investors tracking the Vietnamese financial sector, and may attract incremental capital flows into bank equities — marginally relevant to VN-Index composition and sector weighting dynamics.
